00-hello: Agree on a small process before anyone uses it.
Activation approvals and a validated action produce an inspectable result.
01-order-payment: Offer customers a payment they can trust, without giving up clear settlement rules.
The customer requests capture in the Payment Instruction after delivery; each instruction keeps its own approvals and settlement state.
02-reseller-ledger: Pay partners for money actually collected, including later corrections.
Independent orders feed confirmed net payments into a commission ledger.
03-milestone-payments: Release money as each part of a project is accepted.
Each milestone has its own payment and explicit readiness checks.
04-bundle-order: Sell a package while keeping each supplier’s service independent.
A Documents clause creates multiple orders from one agreed template.
05-smart-home: Connect a verified check-in to the rental’s payment conditions.
A matching event from a separate property document requests capture; unrelated events do not.
06-membership: Turn a trial into a membership only when the customer chooses it.
Separate period obligations and a termination lifecycle keep ongoing work explicit.
07-booking-amendment: Change a booking without silently replacing its existing payment.
Both parties approve the same amendment before the terms change.
08-participants-agents: Give a representative one job without giving them the principal’s powers.
A frozen party roster binds a real representative identity to explicitly assigned actions.
10-net-settlement: Settle the corrected net amount across approved statements.
Statements determine the obligation; a separate confirmed payment settles it.
11-hello-events: React automatically to a specific business event.
An event binding invokes a reusable action only for a matching event.
12-hello-change: Keep a reaction close to the state it depends on.
A change binding observes a property update and runs the connected action.
13-hello-embedded: Let one process react to work completed in another.
The parent listens to events emitted by an embedded child document.
14-hello-collection: Apply one reaction to every order created under an agreement.
A collection binding listens to matching events from multiple independent children.
15-product: Keep quotes valid when quantities or prices change.
Product actions validate their inputs before updating the agreed product.
16-ledger: Track an obligation through corrections, reservation and settlement.
Ledger entries distinguish what is owed, reserved and confirmed as settled.
17-termination: End a relationship without abandoning outstanding work.
The document winds down first and terminates only after its obligations finish.
18-amendments: Give both parties control over changes to agreed terms.
Amendments collect approvals for one exact proposed revision.
19-instruction-with-clauses: Add business-specific behavior to an ordinary payment document.
A standard Payment Instruction composes with a reusable clause while preserving its party roster.
20-status-branch: Make the permitted next actions clear in a repair process.
State transitions follow the agreed graph and reject invalid paths.
21-myos-customer: Describe a customer payment and its business conditions in one shared process.
The customer-payment specialization uses the same correlated request and guarantor-confirmation protocol.
22-myos-account: Coordinate a payment between distinct MyOS accounts.
Customer, seller and test guarantor act through their own authorized routes.
23-manual-bank: Record a bank transfer without claiming an unverified request is a payment.
The designated recipient confirms receipt explicitly.
24-acme-bank: Connect a bank-specific preparation flow to common payment rules.
The example separates preparation, capture and refund requests from provider outcomes.
25-shipping: Keep order delivery and carrier confirmation in agreement.
A separate shipping document distinguishes shipment and address-change requests from confirmed outcomes.
26-timers: Schedule follow-ups and cancel reminders when the process changes.
Signed time drives first-event and latest-event timers; it is not a browser animation.
27-payment-protocol: Handle uncertain and failed payment outcomes without losing the request history.
Correlated requests, retries and reconciliation keep intent separate from confirmation.
28-payment-controls: Apply payment limits and cancellation rules consistently.
The protocol checks policy while retaining the distinction between requests and authoritative results.
29-payment-rejection: Stop an unacceptable payment before its normal flow can proceed.
Instruction rejection prevents later payment operations from continuing.
